_readme: Batch input for generating the game's art. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every
fact about an asset: its prompt, its sizes, its format and where the file goes.
docs/ART.md is the prose companion — it explains the reasoning and the house rules and
deliberately does NOT restate a size or a prompt body, because a fact kept in two places
drifts. (BALANCE.md's header records what that costs; it happened three times there.)
To build one prompt, concatenate the fields named in `compose`, separated by blank lines,
in that order. `style` is stored ONCE and never edited per asset — a set that looks like
five different artists is almost always somebody tidying the style wording between images.
Assets with "palette": true get `palette` inserted where `compose` says.
Generate at `generate`, downscale to `ship`, never upscale. Write the original to
`originalsDir` (outside web/public, gitignored) and the shipped file to `out`.
Alongside every original write <name>.json recording model, full prompt, seed and date —
you will want a matching asset in six months and will not remember.
style: Melancholic 1980s anime watercolour magazine illustration. Watercolour wash with visible paper grain, soft feathered edges, muted desaturated palette, subtle ink linework kept thin and broken. Low-key chiaroscuro firelight OR soft overcast daylight — one or the other, never both. Simplified background, selective detail: render one focal area crisply and let everything else dissolve into wash. Post-apocalyptic solarpunk: a mechanically sophisticated built world of the recent past going green, never rustic fantasy and never a primeval wilderness — dense electromechanical equipment, weathered concrete, salvaged late-20th-century computer hardware, cable and steel tangled with vines. Overgrown, quiet, nobody in a hurry. No overlaid text, no logos, no watermark, no signature, no UI, no border or frame.
palette: Palette anchors: deep teal sky #2b6f74, pale sage haze #b7cbb0, dark canopy green #12301f, bark brown #3a2f26, warm brass #a8834d, lamp gold #e0c07a, bone #ecdfba. Salvage and ruin, which should carry as much of the frame as the greenery does: oxidised verdigris #5f8f80, salvaged amber #d9a25a, weathered concrete #537066, dead plastic #33453e, charred wreck #241c17.
style_sprite: Semi-chibi anime sprite in a melancholic 1980s anime watercolour magazine style. Watercolour wash with visible paper grain and a muted desaturated palette, but kept CRISP: a clean readable silhouette, edges that hold rather than feather away, thin broken ink linework, flat-on with no perspective and no ground shadow. Even soft light across the whole figure — no chiaroscuro, no single dramatic light source. Mechanically sophisticated cassette-futurist solarpunk, overgrown and quiet — machinery first, bamboo and cord as repairs rather than the technology itself. No text, no logos, no watermark, no signature, no UI, no border or frame.
_style_note: There are exactly TWO style blocks and there must never be a third.
`style` is for illustrations — covers, backgrounds, title. It says 'render one focal area
crisply and let everything else dissolve into wash', which is right for a painting seen
`style_sprite` is for anything cut out and drawn small: crew, creatures, props, item
icons. It exists because that one instruction is actively wrong for a sprite — an edge
that dissolves has no silhouette, and a silhouette is the entire readability budget of a
figure drawn 40 pixels tall. The chiaroscuro clause has to go too: a sprite lit from
low-left in the sheet will fight whatever light the scene puts it in.
Assets select one with "style_use": "sprite". Textures (paper grain, wash, vignette) use
neither and set "style_use": "none" — an illustration style block pasted over a texture
prompt is how you get subject matter in your paper grain.

subject_canon._note: Paste `tower` verbatim into any prompt showing the tower from outside. These are not stylistic preferences — they are what web/src/engine/scene.ts actually draws, and RENDERER.md records why. Getting them wrong is the one error that survives into every asset at once.
subject_canon.tower: The tower walks on SIX slender articulated legs arranged as three mechanical bogies, each with a near and rear limb. It uses an alternating tripod gait: three feet carry the hull while their partners advance, then the load swaps diagonally. Each leg is a broad two-link Z mechanism with a circular servo joint, never a human knee or bird's backward hock. Rear-plane legs sit slightly higher and darker; the outer bogies splay while the middle pair braces the hull. The legs are thin relative to the hull so the six-limbed silhouette reads as a walking machine, not a row of stilts or a pipe rack.
subject_canon.roof: A row of low planters runs the full width of the roof: the tower's own garden, spilling greenery over the roof lip. NO sails, no canopy panels, no masts, no banners, no flags.
subject_canon.hull: A long horizontal hull of bamboo, salvaged timber and scavenged panelling — yellowed beige computer casings, perforated rack steel, patched plastic — open to the viewer in cross-section like a doll's house, its floors stacked as shallow horizontal bands of small lit rooms with tiny figures inside. Cable runs and coloured patch leads thread between the floors. A heavy base beam runs under the hull where the legs meet it.
subject_canon.tech: The old world here is mechanically sophisticated late-20th-century cassette-futurism, salvaged and overgrown: dense banks of relays and servos, rotary drums, brass linkages, perforated metal housings, instrument clusters, beige and off-white moulded plastic gone yellow with age, CRT monitors and terminals, chunky keycaps, ribbon cable and coloured patch leads, exposed circuit boards, tape reels, steel racks and small indicator lamps. A screen that is lit glows as a flat amber or phosphor-green rectangle with faint scanlines — never legible text, never a recognisable logo or interface. Machinery is the first read; bamboo, timber and cord are structural repairs and human additions, not substitutes for technology. Everything is scuffed, sun-bleached and half-swallowed by growth, with vines threaded through grilles and moss on control cabinets. This is the point of the setting: where you would otherwise draw a bare rock, plain tree trunk or handmade wooden contraption, prefer a concrete edge, dead server rack, geared actuator or bundle of cable under moss. Overgrown MECHANICAL TECH, not wilderness, rustic fantasy, sleek biotech or glossy science fiction.
subject_canon.crew: The crew are drawn compact semi-chibi: 2.5 to 2.75 heads tall from crown to sole, with heads and hair silhouettes about 35% larger than realistic anime proportions, shorter torsos, forearms, thighs and shins, and slightly oversized readable hands and boots. They are still unmistakably ADULT workers, never full chibi, children, dolls or mascots: retain adult builds, jawlines, necks and work-worn posture. Simplified anime faces with small, restrained features; at sprite size an eye is one mark. Practical layered working clothes, jungle-worn, sleeves pushed up, soft earth and sage tones with one warmer accent each. Scavenged kit rather than issued kit: one or two recognisable pieces per person such as a webbing harness, hand lamp, patch-lead coil or old headset; simplify secondary straps, pouches and circuitry into broad readable shapes. Adults at work, of visibly different builds, ages and origins.
subject_canon.crew_tone: Warmth, not comedy. This is a melancholy game and semi-chibi is here to make small figures legible and likeable, not to make them funny. No gag expressions, no sweat-drops, no speed lines, no exaggerated squash-and-stretch, no wide anime grins. Faces are calm, tired, absorbed in a task. Nobody poses, nobody salutes, nobody holds a weapon like a hero: DECISIONS.md §8 is defenders rather than soldiers, and it binds the art.
subject_canon.creature: Creatures are ANIMALS defending their territory, not monsters and not a target gallery. Semi-chibi in the same register as the crew: rounded, slightly large-headed, softened proportions, readable silhouette first. Give each one a real animal's calm — a root borer is a beetle doing a beetle thing. No snarls, no bared fangs, no glowing eyes, no aggressive rearing poses, no armour plating, no spikes added for menace. They can be big and they can be unsettling; they must never look evil.

budget._note: 40 MiB hard ceiling for shipped art. This is headroom, not a target: keep opaque paintings as quality-tuned WebP, alpha sheets indexed and optimized, and never ship full-resolution sources. `make release` prints the size. Prefer a larger asset only when live comparison shows that the smaller derivative loses material readability.

assets.subject: An enormous walking garden-tower of bamboo and salvaged timber, seen from the side and slightly below, striding through the overgrown remains of a city. {hull} {tower} {roof} {tech} Three feet planted in an alternating tripod stance while their three partners advance. Around and behind it: collapsed concrete storeys, a leaning pylon, dead signage gone blank, all going green. Soft overcast light, mist between the trunks and the ruins.
assets.composition: Tower left of centre and small against a huge horizon. Leave the top third quiet — a title will sit there. Landscape 5:4.

Overcast, early morning, mist in the middle distance.

assets.usedBy: title screen background
assets.subject: INTERIOR. One lamplit deck inside the walking tower at night, seen from the side in cross-section. Two crew sitting at a low table, small in frame, sharing a meal. {crew} {crew_tone} {tech} Bamboo racks and hanging tools beside a salvaged equipment rack: a dead CRT terminal used as a shelf, one small screen still lit amber in the corner, patch leads looped on a hook, a potted cutting on top of a beige casing. A cooking pot. Warm firelight from a single lamp; everything beyond its reach dissolves into dark wash. Through a gap in the timber, black jungle.
assets.composition: Lamp low-left, the dark two-thirds of the frame doing the work. 16:9.
assets._note: No tower exterior here, so no leg or roof canon needed. Ship size is above generate size deliberately: this sits behind a title at full screen and is the one place softness reads as atmosphere. If your tool does 2048 wide, use it.

assets.usedBy: behind the arrival card — the ending a run is trying to reach
assets.subject: Dawn at the coast. The walking garden-tower stopped on a headland above pale flat water, still, its legs folded under it. {tower} {roof} {tech} Salt grass, and a few half-buried concrete stumps and a leaning aerial mast along the shoreline, softened by grass rather than dramatic. First light on its flank. Nothing threatening — the end of a very long walk.
assets.composition: Tower right of centre, low horizon, most of the frame given to sky. 16:9.

assets.usedBy: behind the loss card
assets.subject: The same walking garden-tower, dark and motionless, being taken back by the jungle. Vines through its open flank, saplings on its roof, one leg buckled under it, its screens dead and its cable runs hanging loose and furred with moss. {tower} {roof} {tech} Flat overcast light. No fire, no drama — just green closing over something that stopped, the same way it closed over the city around it.
assets.composition: Tower centred and small, canopy crowding in from every edge. 16:9.

assets.subject: Seamless tileable cold-press watercolour paper texture. Greyscale only, no subject matter, no objects, no composition. Even fine tooth across the whole square, no dark blotches, no visible seam at any edge, no vignette, no lighting. A flat scan of blank paper.
assets._note: style_use is "none" on purpose: the illustration style block would put subject matter into a texture. Verify tiling by laying it out 2×2 and looking for the seam before shipping.

assets.subject: Ten separate side-on scenery props in a grid, evenly spaced, each isolated with clear empty space around it and its base sitting on a common baseline: a jungle tree; a fern; a hanging vine; a mossy chunk of broken concrete kerb; a piece of bleached driftwood; a cracked salt-pan crust; a ruined concrete pillar with rebar showing, overgrown; a toppled perforated-steel server rack with its beige machines still in it, ferns growing through the gaps; a heap of dead CRT monitors and terminals with yellowed plastic, screens blank and dusty, one with a sapling out of it; a rusted vehicle wreck half-swallowed by growth. {tech} Each drawn flat-on from the side, no perspective, no ground shadow.
assets.composition: Ten props in a 5x2 grid on a FLAT MAGENTA #FF00FF background. Even spacing, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the image edges.
assets._note: One painting pass matches itself far better than ten separate ones — that is the whole reason this is a sheet. Cut apart and repack after keying out the magenta. Six of the ten are salvage rather than greenery on purpose: the terrain the game actually generates is Drowned Street, Ruin Field, Collapsed District and Flooded Boulevard, so a prop set that is mostly trees and rocks would describe a different world from the one underfoot.

assets.subject: Twenty-four separate side-on cutaway room-interior dressings in the exact cell order given, all built from salvaged late-20th-century computing and dense electromechanical machinery. {tech} Draw only furnishings and machinery, never the room shell, floor plate, roof, exterior crown, exterior weapon barrel, people, labels or UI. The rooms are: a purely electromechanical amber capacitor-heart in a perforated server chassis, with relay banks, flywheel and braided root-like cable bundles but NO seed, pod, fruit, flower, bulb or organic core; a salvage rig with sorting gantry, magnetic grab, rack-steel bins and CRT inspection station; a bunk background with lockers, folded blankets, headset hooks and patched bags, leaving hammock space clear; a burner with refractory firebox housing, heat exchanger and duct controls, no flame or smoke; a canteen with counter, communal pot, shelves and terminal, leaving the hearth clear; a cellwright bench assembling chunky battery packs beside a charger rack; a cutter-arm winch room with cable drums, hydraulic pump and controls, no exterior arm; a fiber comb with toothed drums, rollers and skeins; a fitter bench with stepper motors, gears, circuit boards and tools; an instrumented hydroponic garden with resin vessels, irrigation manifold and sensor terminals; a kitbench with toolrolls, harness webbing, lamps and buckles; a lantern-mast switch room with cable reels, ceramic switches and spare lamps, no exterior mast; a bamboo mill with feed rollers, guarded splitting wheel and finished-pole rack; a resonance-array room with flywheel, tuned resonator drums, striker bank and an abstract-trace CRT, no ordnance cues; a resonator works with compact lathe, diaphragm jig, laminating press and drum cores, no seed imagery; a ropery with twisting wheels, hooks and coils; a storeroom with four open shelf bays holding rack steel, yellowed plastic and cable; a sun-forge with shielded crucible, induction coils and dark control CRT; a cell-bank rack with bus bars and empty cell slots; a dart-battery breech with crank and dart magazine but no exterior barrel; a root-ward cabinet with downward spike driver, grounded copper coils and four-spike rack; a tanglenet room with folded net canister, reel and tensioner; a thorn-gun breech with bamboo feed wheel but no exterior barrel; a thornwright bench with drill press, sharpening wheel and unfinished-dart trays. Keep every screen blank or abstract and every lamp unlit so live state can be drawn over it. Distinct readable silhouettes and negative spaces, but one coherent tower assembled by the same people.
assets.composition: Three precise 4x2 source grids on perfectly FLAT MAGENTA #FF00FF backgrounds, eight rooms per source sheet in sourceSheets order. Every cell equal with strong empty gutters, one dressing centred in each cell on a shared baseline, below 82% of cell height. Nothing crosses a boundary or touches an edge. Flat side view, no perspective, no ground shadow.
assets._note: The three source sheets keep a 24-room prompt legible to the generator; process_art.py keys and packs them into one texture. This is interior dressing, not replacement state art: the renderer draws active motion and warmth, idle dimming, backed-up stock, damage, and a deterministic broken composite for destroyed rooms above or from the same cell. The room cell set is enforced against assets/data/rooms/*.ron.

assets.subject: Twenty-four distinct full-cell architectural backings for the tower's rooms, built as one coherent family from salvaged late-20th-century computing, rack steel, ceramic electrical hardware and overgrown mechanical infrastructure. {tech} These are ROOM SHELLS ONLY: every cell must be a single connected opaque cutaway interior skin comprising its ceiling liner, full back wall, both side jambs and floor or deck surface. Fill the whole room footprint and reserve the middle foreground for the separate furnishing atlas. Give every named room a memorable architectural identity rather than changing only its colour: bunk has quilted acoustic insulation, personal hooks and rounded sleeping-car ribs; burner has soot-dark refractory brick, broad heat shielding and fat duct collars; canteen has scrubbed enamel wall panels, tiled splashback and a warm copper flue chase; cellwright has insulated battery alcoves, ceramic bus channels and acid-resistant green enamel; cutter arm has massive diagonal recoil braces, hose trunks and a reinforced exterior mounting bulkhead; fiber comb has long lint screens, toothed guard motifs and thread-guide rails; fitter has a precise pegboard-like tool wall, articulated task-light rails and dense service sockets; garden has wet glazed panels, irrigation channels, hanging root trays and restrained living moss; kitbench has compact locker bays, harness rails and rounded field-case panels; lantern mast has a tall switchboard spine, porcelain knife-switch silhouettes and vertical cable risers; mill has heavy ribbed guards, a wide feed-mouth frame and amber sawdust extraction channels; resonance array has concentric acoustic baffles, tuned radial braces and waveform-like abstract panel geometry with no text; resonator works has circular diaphragm racks, copper-lined isolation panels and a compact clean-machine bay; ropery has sweeping tension-rail arcs, hook rows and a long horizontal twisting corridor; storeroom has deep numbered-shape bays with no legible writing, tie-down grids and a broad loading sill; sun forge has black ceramic heat tiles, a shielded crucible recess and pale refractory ribs; Heartseed has a rounded amber capacitor vault, braided trunk conduits and an unusually monumental central frame, with NO seed, pod, fruit, flower, bulb or organic core; salvage rig has scarred industrial plating, a broad ground-access hatch, magnetic-rail braces and mismatched recovered panels; cell bank has a disciplined wall of empty dark battery vaults and thick insulated bus trunks; dart battery has a compact armoured embrasure, recoil rails and protected ammunition channels but no weapon barrel; root ward has downward-pointing copper grounding geometry, spike guide channels and a reinforced lower deck; tanglenet has a broad circular reel recess, tension-web ribs and orange safety patches; thorn gun has a rugged feed-channel bulkhead, compact recoil cradle and violet cable accents but no barrel; thornwright has a dense drilling-bay frame, narrow sharpening guards and ordered material channels. Category colours are restrained splashes, never flat washes. No two rooms may share the same large silhouette or wall-panel rhythm. All screens and state lamps remain blank and dark.
assets.composition: Three precise PORTRAIT 2-column by 4-row source grids on perfectly FLAT MAGENTA #FF00FF backgrounds, eight named shells per source sheet in sourceSheets row-major order. Every grid cell is equal and contains exactly one orthographic side-on landscape room backing as a single connected rectangular silhouette. The painted shell itself must fill at least 94% of its usable width and 82% of its usable height, with an even magenta isolation gutter outside it; within the shell there are NO magenta holes, transparent bare-wall gaps, floating boxes, detached lines or empty bands. Architecture runs cleanly to all four shell edges so it can be resized to the exact runtime room rectangle. Architecture only: no benches, work machines, loose items, people, labels, UI, stock, exterior crowns, weapons, fire, smoke, damage, glows or active lights. Flat side view, no perspective and no cast ground shadow.
assets._note: Optional specificity layer with the exact rooms-atlas UV rectangles. process_art.py removes each keyed source-cell gutter and registers the connected backing across its complete destination rectangle, so no generic wall shows through behind furnishings. Painted art owns room-specific material, silhouette, exact accent colours and architectural character; renderer state may multiply brightness but must not replace or flatten those authored hues. The renderer owns furnishings, activity, progress, charge, inventory, occupancy, lamps, damage, destruction, fire and smoke. Absence of this optional atlas must retain the category-shell fallback.

assets.subject: A modular architecture kit for the tower's complete room cells and exterior machinery, built from the same salvaged late-20th-century cassette-futurist materials as the room furnishings. {tech} The FIRST TWO ROWS are eight full rectangular side-on cutaway ROOM SHELL BACKINGS in this exact order: Heart, Intake, Production, Storage; Energy, Defence, Quarters, fallback. Each is a complete inhabited architectural cell with an opaque painted ceiling liner, back wall, floor or deck skin, side jambs, mounting rails, cable and pipe runs, vents, brackets and restrained category-colour patches. Heart is a rounded capacitor vault with braided trunk conduits; Intake has hydraulic feeds, dirt guards and intake ducting; Production has heavy machine mounts, tool power and workshop extraction; Storage has shelf rails, tie-downs and abstract inventory-plate shapes with no legible marks; Energy has ceramic busbars, insulators and shielded cable channels; Defence has compact armour, recoil bracing and protected service runs; Quarters has fabric insulation, lockers, hooks and softer rounded framing; fallback is neutral rack steel and patch panels. Keep the middle and lower furnishing zone lower-contrast so the separate room-specific machinery remains readable above it. The LAST TWO ROWS are isolated transparent exterior crown components in this exact order: a compact electromechanical Heart capacitor cap with no seed or organic core; a narrow hydroponic sensor trellis; an EMPTY cell-bank rack with dark glass housings; a burner's broad twin heat-exchanger stack; a single workshop extraction vent; a long jointed cutter boom only, with no interior winch room; a compact mechanical defence barrel and receiver; and one completely empty spare cell. All screens and lamps are blank and dark. Never draw a whole tower, walker, room furnishing or person.
assets.composition: One precise 4x4 grid on a perfectly FLAT uniform MAGENTA #FF00FF chroma-key background. Every grid cell is exactly equal and nothing crosses a boundary. In rows 1 and 2, each shell is a coherent opaque rectangular cutaway panel that fills about 94% of its cell width and height, leaving only a narrow even magenta isolation gutter; there must be NO magenta holes, transparent bare-wall gaps, detached floating boxes or empty bands inside a shell. Ceiling, side walls, back wall and deck all connect into one full-cell silhouette.
